title: Post-POC: Next Steps Decision Matrix and Risk Playbook — Acme Health AI POC
content:
Executive summary:

This document captures the readout for the Acme Health POC (speech-to-structured-summary pipeline), highlights measurable outcomes, and presents a compact decision matrix plus a risk playbook for recommended next steps. The POC ran for 4 weeks (internal infra + Redwood hosted API fallback), processed ~4,200 clinical audio minutes, and exercised edge cases for short/long sessions and noisy audio.

High-level outcome: technically feasible with modest model tuning and caching; business impact potential is meaningful (>35% time savings for clinicians on note prep in our simulated workload) but operationalization requires choices about deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), quantization & latency trade-offs, and integration with Acme’s PHI controls.

Goals and success criteria (as agreed in kickoff):
- Accuracy: structured-field extraction F1 >= 0.78 on annotated holdout.
- Latency: end-to-end per-session (audio->summary) mean <= 8s for sessions <120s.
- Cost: average per-minute inference cost <= $0.85 for steady-state (target for Dedicated).
- Security: no PHI persisted outside customer environment when in Private mode.

POC results (technical):
- Accuracy: achieved F1=0.80 for primary fields after prompt-tuning + small label mapping; secondary fields still at F1=0.63.
- Latency: Redwood hosted baseline (standard model) mean 6.1s for short sessions; optimized pipeline (quantized model + batching + KV caching) on Dedicated reached 4.2s median but tail (95th) remained at ~12s for very noisy 10+ minute sessions.
- Throughput: peak concurrent sessions supported on a single Dedicated pod (p3-equivalent) ~18 sessions with batching window 40ms.
- Cost: hosted baseline cost was $1.12/min (higher than target); Dedicated estimation (based on our stress tests and RWI cost model) projects $0.62–$0.72/min when amortized.
- Integration: Live demo successfully integrated with Acme EHR dev sandbox; PHI redaction hooks required minor client-side changes.

POC results (business):
- Usability readout with 6 clinician testers: average Likert improvement +2.5 for time-to-note, but desire for targeted edit controls and audit trails.
- Value signal: in sim workload, projected 4–6 FTE equivalents of clinician time saved per 100 clinicians for note prep.
- Adoption risks surfaced: trust in output quality, regulatory/auditability concerns, and SLA expectations for real-time workflows.

Key learnings and constraints:
- Model switching: for noisy long sessions, a higher-capacity variant outperforms quantized smaller models — fallback routing is essential to maintain quality on edge cases.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduced repeated-token costs by ~28% for multi-part sessions (clinician dictation with corrections).
- Batching/Windowing: aggressive batching improves throughput cost but increases tail latency; tuning required by customer SLA.
- Data residency: Acme requires that audio and final structured outputs remain inside a VPC; this pushes the likely path toward Private deployment or Dedicated in their VPC.

Decision matrix (3 recommended paths):
- Option A — Hosted (fastest time-to-market): Redwood hosted API, model: standard LLM with prompt-fine-tuning, add on-client redaction and audit logging. Pros: minimal ops, fastest rollout (4–6 weeks). Cons: cost high, does not meet Acme PHI residency requirement without Private mode.
- Option B — Dedicated (balanced): Reserved Dedicated capacity in a Redwood VPC region close to Acme, quantized model for steady-state, higher-capacity fallback variant for noisy cases, rollout with canary routes. Pros: meets latency & cost targets, simpler integration than Private. Cons: requires contract/commit, some changes to network/firewall rules.
- Option C — Private on-prem/VPC (compliant): Full Private deployment with customer-controlled data plane, KMS/HSM integration, local inference for PHI. Pros: satisfies compliance, full control. Cons: longest setup (8–14 weeks), higher lift (ops + infra), initial cost higher but predictable.

Decision matrix summary (qualitative):
- If PHI residency is non-negotiable => Option C.
- If cost predictability + lower ops burden prioritized => Option B.
- If Acme wants immediate pilot without PHI-level data => Option A for limited demo only.

Recommended next steps (priority + owner + timeline):
1) Contract track & procurement alignment (Owner: Jordan Lee) — 2 weeks. Prepare Dedicated pricing sheet and PO-ready appendix.
2) Security & compliance due diligence (Owner: Priya Kapoor) — 3 weeks. Implement minimal HIPAA control checklist and run data flow diagram with Acme security.
3) Technical runbook for deployment modes (Owner: Ethan Ross) — 2 weeks. Include canary rollout plan, automated fallback routing, monitoring hooks.
4) Engineering sprint: Productionization epic (Owner: Solutions Eng leads: Mariana Silva) — 4 sprints (8 weeks) for Dedicated deployment path. Deliverables: model pinning, batching profiles, KV cache tuning, cost telemetry.
5) Clinician feedback loop & acceptance tests (Owner: Product-Liaison Sofia Martinez) — ongoing across sprints, first acceptance gate at sprint 3.

Risk playbook (top risks, triggers, mitigations):
- R1: PHI breach / data residency violation
  Trigger: any audio stored outside customer-controlled storage or logs containing raw audio.
  Mitigation: force Private mode for any PHI data; disable host-side logs of raw audio; encryption at rest & transit; audit logs retention policy.
  Owner: Priya Kapoor

- R2: Quality regression after quantization
  Trigger: F1 drop >0.05 on nightly evals or clinician-reported failures >10/day.
  Mitigation: keep a fallback high-capacity variant with automated routing; regression alerting and automatic rollback to prior pinned model.
  Owner: Ethan Ross

- R3: Latency SLA misses during peak load
  Trigger: 95th percentile session latency >12s for >5% of requests for 30 minutes.
  Mitigation: autoscaling policy to add burst capacity, reduce batching window, initiate graceful degradation (switch to lower-latency template responses), notify on-call SRE.
  Owner: Site Reliability Engineer (TBD)

Rollback/playbook highlights:
- Implement a one-click rollback to previously pinned model version for both hosted and dedicated pipelines.
- Canary window 48 hours; if quality metrics degrade, auto-fallback and create incident.
- Pre-approved incident runbook for clinician-impacting regressions that includes communication templates for Acme product owners and clinicians.

Open questions (from workshop & demos):
- Legal: Is a hybrid approach acceptable where audio capture occurs in-customer but derived structured payloads are sent to hosted analytics? (Awaiting legal confirmation from Acme by 2025-03-10).
- Ops: Which network architecture will Acme approve for Dedicated VPC peering? (Security kickoff scheduled 2025-03-05).
- Product: Which secondary fields are mandatory for go/no-go (currently F1 low)? Product to provide prioritized list by 2025-03-07.

Appendix (notes from demo workshop, 2025-02-26):
- Clinician demo notes: request for per-field confidence scores and quick-edit inline UI—product to scope.
- Integration notes: EHR sandbox required token rotation every 7 days; we validated refresh flow.
- Cost sensitivity: Acme finance asked for 6-, 12-, 24-month cost projections; attached cost model (linked artifact).

Attachment & immediate asks for Acme:
- Request: confirm target deployment mode (A/B/C) by 2025-03-12 so we can lock resource calendar.
- Request: sign non-production data transfer addendum for demo data flow within 1 week to proceed with Dedicated sandbox deployment.

Summary recommendation (concise):
- Proceed with Option B (Dedicated in-customer VPC region) as the primary path: balances cost, latency, and speed-to-value while meeting most compliance needs. Parallel work: start privacy/legal conversations to validate if Private (Option C) is required for full production. Begin procurement and security due-diligence in the next 2 weeks.

Document history & ownership:
- Author: Mariana Silva (solutions-eng lead)
- Primary reviewers: Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Ross, Sofia Martinez
- Next review: internal exec readout scheduled 2025-03-05

End of document.
